checks.note: Residual 0.029 against a noise floor of 0.0256, both on radial-diam-8.58, the upper fillet's ring. The 0.003 over the floor is rotational tessellation: rendered at $fn = 105, the reference's own export setting, this part scores exactly the 0.026 floor. It is not rendered at 105, because $fn belongs to diff_params.scad and the floor does not move.

The only part whose reference compares to itself exactly, so its 0.006 mm was real, and it is bbox alone, every other check being under 6e-7. The rim is a 105-gon whose top and bottom rings are staggered by half a facet, giving 210 extreme positions at 0.857143 deg: x lands on one at 52.500 and y falls midway, so 52.5 * (1 - cos(180/210)) = 0.0058747, the measured delta to eight digits. The tolerance is 0.007, not the 0.006 that would just clear it: a check that passes by 0.000125 mm is one edit to DISK_OD or $fn away from a failure that says nothing. compare has no --ignore-bbox and no per-check tolerance, so for a bounding-box artifact a tolerance is the only lever. Its real defect was invisible to compare: the slot cuts met the recess floor exactly on the plane z = 0.200, and CGAL does not merge two voids that meet on a plane, which left a zero-thickness membrane across every slot. Surface area caught it (3781 mm2 against the reference's 3291) and dist charged 0.35 mm for it. When a cut has to land on a face, give it a second cutter that crosses the face instead.

Residual 0.038 on radial-diam-23.68, the GT2 flank: at the default 0.05 bin the whole flank merges into one run of 8439 vertices whose mean falls in a 0.058 mm gap in the model's flank sampling. The reference has no vertex at its own run mean either, and scores 0.044 against itself. The sculpted under-flange web is modeled as a cone, which the ignore ranges cover.

The added 16.8..17.05 band masks the reference's own bottom face: 1366 vertices at z = 0.000000 forming a 27-gon on diameter 17.000, of which 66 facets are exact reversed duplicates over a 97-degree sector, a zero-thickness sheet. It read 1.075 mm.

The only part whose 0.768 mm was a real departure rather than a phantom of the tolerance, and it is deliberate. This part blunts its tooth tips to the reference's land rather than to the reference's diameter: on the shared crown's shallower tooth form the reference's diameter 43.500 would leave a 0.031 mm land, a sharp tip with a matching number, so the wider blunt is cut instead and the OD comes out 0.785 under. It is pinned as a deviation rather than waved through by a loose tol, because the departure has a value and re-typing the old diameter must fail this check too. Both transverse dims carry it; the axial dim is unaffected. 0.02 of drift is allowed, with 0.768 rather than the OD's own 0.785, because the gear's transverse extent is set by the land corners of the tooth nearest the axis, which move with the flank tessellation. What remains outside the deviation is 0.025 mm on radial-diam-23.76, the shared bevel crown's flank, against a self-comparison floor of 0.016. The render is the solid, buildable shaft (wall_holes false) and the reference carries twelve 0.2 mm holes on diameter 15.5; the 15.3..15.7 band masks that ring.

This reference is two overlapping closed solids, cage and bevel crown, and neither can be stripped: --keep 0 would delete the whole crown. The ignore ranges are its buried faces and mesher ladders: the crown's back face at z 15.448 (which read 0.562 mm), the heel root diameter 36.717 buried inside the cage's 36.997, that same circle seen as a plane, and the tooth-flank ladder over z 18.358..20.391. The band widened to 25.25 covers the 23 to 28 fillet's ring ladder, whose self-noise alone is 0.074.

The 1.500 mm was the crown solid's buried bottom edge at z 18.500, a knife edge 2 mm inside the merged part's material, which no correct model can carry a vertex on. The 17.250 plane range is the tessellation seam where the diameter 27 wall's outline drops from 430 points to 308 with the diameter and area unchanged.

The two housings are held to a stricter contract than the rest. compare matches feature planes and diameters, so a body can satisfy every mating interface while its shell is nothing like the reference: Body A passed its interface checks at 2.43x the reference's material. They are gated on dist, a two-sided surface distance, which catches a missing feature or a wrong hole shape. Body B joins when it is rebuilt as a faithful recreation.

Slice stations are in each render's own frame, and the check reads the render the earlier jobs wrote, so it must run after them. 720-003 is authored in its reference's coordinates, spanning z 17.500 to 27.750, so the station is 23.5, the part-local 6.0 plus the part's own base: it finds 40 on both meshes, and the reference gives 40 at every station from 20.0 to 27.0. Body B's axes both sit at -21, so its center is written --center=-21,21: a negative value in the spaced form is read as a flag.

Mating diameters on the housings, stated directly in terms a reader can check by eye. Body B's shaft bore is on X, the J4 axis, not on Y; the former y = -48.5 station sampled the mating rim and could never have found a seat.

The assembly is exported to CSG rather than STL: that evaluates every parameter and assertion (the L4 split, the axis intersection) in seconds, where meshing the union of nine parts, three of them involute bevel gears, takes minutes and checks nothing extra. Render it to STL by hand to look at it: openscad -o out/assembly.stl -D config='"revised"' diff_assembly.scad.
The arm composition, which holds Body A to the forearm skin.
The External pulleys are 400-EndArm's parts, but they are the elbow half of the same DC-12 train, so they are verified here too.
The outer External pulley's hub: the 8 mm rod, and the M3 nut (5.5 across flats) in the slot on 180 deg, whose 5.5 runs along Y.
720-001 is exported turned onto +Y: its own (x, y, z) lies at (x, z, -y).
